Cam York practised on Monday, and Rick Tocchet said he could return on Tuesday or Wednesday. The Flyers play in Washington the next night.
Adam Fantilli won Saturday's game against Vegas with a power-play goal in overtime. It was Columbus' first power-play goal in 23 chances.
Columbus is without Ivan Provorov, Dante Fabbro and Isac Lundestrom. Dan Vladar and Jet Greaves are the likely starters.
records: The Flyers' 0-6-3 start was the worst in franchise history. They score 1.85 goals a game, 32nd in the league.

en.title: Vegas tries to stop a three-game slide as Marner returns
en.deck: Vegas has lost a season-high three straight and gets Mitch Marner back after he missed two games for the birth of his second child. Ottawa opens a five-game road trip at 8-4-0, three October wins away from matching its club record. The market makes Vegas a clearer favourite than the model does.
news: Marner returned to practice on Monday and is expected to play. Parker Wotherspoon is out for Vegas.
Thomas Chabot practised in a regular jersey; Travis Green said he is close but may not play on Tuesday. Linus Ullmark and William Eklund are out.
With Ullmark out, Ottawa's net is a question: Samuel Ersson is 0-3-0 with an .835 save percentage, and the model expects Jonas Johansson. No starter is confirmed.
Mark Stone, who leads Vegas with 8 goals and 15 points, says there is no need to panic.
records: Drake Batherson had his third career hat trick in Saturday's 7-4 win over the Rangers and has 11 points in his last 10 games.
Ottawa needs three more October wins to match the club record of nine, set in 2007-08.
Jack Eichel has 13 points in his last 10 games. Vegas is 5-2-0 at home.
The last six meetings averaged 7.7 goals, and 10 of Vegas' 13 games have gone over 5.5.
betting: Market: Golden Knights 1.65, Senators 2.28, about 58–42 without the margin. The model has 55–45, a little warmer on Ottawa.

en.title: Vancouver is one loss from tying its worst streak ever
en.deck: The Canucks have lost 10 straight, and another defeat would tie the franchise record of 11 set last season. They allow 4.62 goals a game, the most in the league. Anaheim ended its own five-game skid on Saturday, and the model, like the market, has the Ducks as a clear favourite.
news: Manny Malhotra said the start against Minnesota on Sunday was positive in everything but the score; Vancouver was then outshot 29-7 over the last 40 minutes.

Kevin Lankinen is winless in eight appearances with an .807 save percentage. Daily Faceoff projects Leevi Merilainen, while the model's goalie feed still leans to Lankinen. Thatcher Demko is out after hip surgery.
Brock Boeser called the team's play embarrassing after a 5-2 loss to Detroit, then ended his goal drought on Sunday.
Anaheim is without Troy Terry, Ryan Poehling, Pavel Mintyukov and Ian Moore. Lukas Dostal is the likely starter.
records: Anaheim beat Philadelphia 5-4 from 2-0 down. Beckett Sennecke's power-play winner ended an 0-for-15 drought, and Tristan Luneau had his first three-point game.
Leo Carlsson leads Anaheim with 13 points (10 assists).
Vancouver went 13-2-0 against Anaheim over the previous four seasons and has won 7 of its last 8 games in Anaheim.
Seven of Vancouver's 10 straight losses have been by two goals or more.
betting: Market: Ducks 1.47, Canucks 2.80, about 66–34 without the margin. The model has 63–37, slightly less sure about Anaheim.
Total: the market prices over 5.5 at 1.53 (about 62%). The model agrees (63%) and projects 6.7 goals, the highest of the night.

en.title: Buffalo opens its California trip searching for second periods
en.deck: The Sabres are winless in three (0-1-2) and minus-11 in second periods this season, near the bottom of the league. Macklin Celebrini has 15 points for San Jose, which lost 6-4 in Boston on Saturday. The model agrees with the market that Buffalo is a modest favourite.

San Jose is without Igor Chernyshov and Quentin Musty; Alexander Wennberg left an Oct. 19 game hurt.
records: Buffalo's power play has three goals in 11 games, 31st in the league. The Sabres are plus-8 in third periods.
